subject.title: exec auto-reviewer re-bills a fresh model completion for every byte-identical repeated exec

question: Should OpenClaw approve a bounded per-reviewer-instance exact-input cache for low-risk allow-once model-backed exec reviewer decisions, and should plugin/harness helper reuse be in scope?
rationale: The source bug is clear, but an identical later exec request would skip a fresh model review, so cache lifetime and sibling-surface scope are security-boundary product intent rather than a purely mechanical repair.

options.title: Approve exact-input per-run memo
options.body: Accept a bounded non-persistent cache in the shared reviewer after real configured-run proof, with helper reuse treated as a separate follow-up if needed.

options.title: Require broader helper coverage
options.body: Keep the issue blocked until plugin or harness helpers that construct reviewers per call either reuse reviewer lifetime or have an explicit out-of-scope decision.

options.title: Keep fresh review semantics
options.body: Reject memoization and accept repeated reviewer model cost to preserve one fresh model review per exec request.

recommendation.title: Approve exact-input per-run memo
recommendation.body: Accept a bounded non-persistent cache in the shared reviewer after real configured-run proof, with helper reuse treated as a separate follow-up if needed.

likelyOwner.reason: The introduced auto-mode/reviewer history makes this the strongest available routing candidate for the approval-boundary decision.
